rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 was REVISE on a gating guardian objection, and the objection was the right question: does `page_components.build_status` ever equal 'deployed'? The landmine table records the SIBLING table's `site_components.build_status` as 'rendered' and NEVER 'deployed', so if page_components matched it, the extracted page-total floor would be permanently inert, my 337-of-366 figure would rest on a predicate matching nothing, and a sqlmock suite would happily certify a guard that never runs. REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, run 2026-08-17: 'deployed' is the DOMINANT value on page_components — 1,575 rows across 617 pages, against approved 85, pending 19, removed 4 — and 617 of 729 pages (84.6%) have at least one deployed row with a non-null rendered_html. The analogy did not transfer; the predicate is live; no code changed for this objection and the query is in grounded_in below.

The other four are acted on in code, not argued away:

1. bug_historian (medium) — the page-total floor's FAIL-OPEN path stood down silently, which is 'indistinguishable from no floor at all on the very incident class this whole bug is about'. It now files a work item, under its OWN type `save_guard_unmeasured` rather than the `save_refused_incomplete` its siblings use, because nothing was refused on that path and a row asserting otherwise is a false claim in a queue a human reads. Producer set (one call site), key shape (`save_guard_unmeasured:<page name>`) and 'no automated consumer, by design' are stated at the constructor per the owner ruling of 2026-08-02 §1, and it carries its own remedy sentence because 'lower the floor' is wrong advice for a threshold that was never consulted. The floor still fails OPEN — reconciling that with its two fail-closed siblings is a behavioural change that deserves its own evidence and must not ride an axis correction.

2. bug_historian (medium) — whether `visibleTextLength` agrees with the page assembler's own `sectionHasVisibleContent`, which the seat correctly said needed a human diff. They DIFFER by construction: parser (dropping script/style/noscript/template/code/pre/svg/iframe/textarea/select/option/head with their content, entities decoded) versus a regex chain (style blocks, script blocks, tags, entities, whitespace) with a >10-char threshold and an explicit runtime-fill escape. Only ONE direction matters — nothing this floor judges as prose-bearing may be droppable by the assembler, or the save is allowed and the assembler drops the content anyway, which is the second silent-drop path the seat was pointing at. MEASURED over all three populations: 6,585 sections in the floor's scope, ZERO droppable by the assembler; 944 in the harmless direction (the floor declines to judge, the assembler keeps). `TestVisibleDefinitionsAgree` now holds it, with a demand control that FAILS on an empty population — because a code reading gives the same answer but cannot see the entity edge case, where content that is almost entirely entities counts ~0 for the regex and >0 for the parser.

3. reuse_agent (medium) — `pruneFloorFromConfig` is pre-existing, `prune_floor.go:412`, and is the idiom both sibling floors already read their config with; it was not introduced here. Answered, nothing changed.

4. reuse_agent (low) — three `*IncomingBySlot` helpers had grown the same shape, and that duplication is HOW the last-write-wins keying defect came to exist in two of them independently. Collapsed onto one `incomingBySlot(sections, measure)`: the keying question ('what does a repeated slot name mean?') answered once, the measure as the parameter — which is also the separation the calibration harness needs.

5. editquality (low) — 'closes a hole' overstated what ships, because my test asserts three named calls and does not generalise the older writer-coverage test's UPDATE-only regex, so a new writer on some other DELETE+INSERT path stays invisible exactly as before. Corrected to 'narrows', visibly in the file header, AND made partly true: `TestEveryFloorEnforcerHasACaller` fails when ANY `enforce…Floor` function in the package has no caller at all, which is the generic 'someone wrote a fourth floor and never wired it' case the claim was reaching for. MUT-293-H proves it bites: leave `enforceSectionComponentFloor` declared and call nothing, and it fails naming the file and the symbol.

Eight mutations now RUN before commit, not planned (A-H, tabulated in NOTES). Whole `actions` package green at `git archive HEAD`, whole repo builds.

--- ROUND 1 RATIONALE FOLLOWS, unchanged ---

bugs_open/293, the residual half of bugs_closed/285's corrected axis - and the half with the volume: 3,603 whole-page rebuild writes against 281 section-edit writes in the same 8 days. The section editor was moved to a visible-text axis on 2026-08-17 (council 3279156b, APPROVED); the whole-page save was deliberately left on the tag-stripped axis because the bug file judged its DELETE+INSERT writes unpairable, so there was no evidence for the path. THAT JUDGEMENT WAS WRONG AND I HAVE THE EVIDENCE NOW.

THE PAIRING, and it is proven rather than assumed. Migration 357's triggers bank OLD.rendered_html on UPDATE *and* DELETE, so an archive row is the content that was live until that moment; the write that followed it is row.rendered_html -> (next archive row for the same page+slot, else the LIVE page_components row). The bug file's candidate (a) guessed the successor was an unarchived INSERT and called the join unprovable. It is not an INSERT: it is the live row, and page_components.created_at is INDEPENDENT evidence the re-insert belongs to that rebuild. 1,123 of 1,254 (page,slot) groups were re-inserted within 60s of their delete, 1,109 within 5s, and - the disconfirming control - ZERO live rows are older than their own last delete, which a wrong join does not produce. POSITIVE CONTROL against a number I did not produce: the same rule applied to op='overwrite' reproduces the other lane's three known refusals with identical figures (684->0, 2,143->16, 684->0) and their tag-stripped repair at 38.1%, and finds a fourth hollowing they had not reported (idea.uk/index/tool-list, 1,118->0 visible).

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SAYS, including the part that did not go my way. On 1,079 exactly-paired rebuild writes the visible axis refuses ZERO - but so does the tag-stripped axis, because no rebuild in the archived window happened to hollow a page. The guard shipped 2026-08-02 and the archive starts 2026-08-09, so every pair is a write the LIVE guard ALLOWED: that makes this population exactly right for measuring FALSE REFUSALS and useless for measuring true catches. So "it would have caught X" is NOT AVAILABLE on this path and I am not claiming it. The case is mechanism, measured prospectively: construct this bug's failure on all 1,079 real sections (delete every word of prose, keep the wrapper markup and the <style>/<script> content) and the retired axis judges 1,060 and ALLOWS the total wipe on 724 of them (68%); the visible axis judges 492 and allows 0. Confirmed by a second, independent instrument (a crude regex, not the parser): 728 of 1,062 sections have over half of what the guard calls "text" inside style/script, 85-89% on some.

THE FALSE-REFUSAL COST, stated as a rate and hand-inspected. Across the wider weak-join population the visible axis would refuse exactly ONE write the guard would actually have judged: robot-hands.com/about/differentiators, 2026-08-11 13:12:30, two rebuilds 96s apart, 3,724->1,554 visible chars. I read both sides - the incoming is a tighter, better-grounded rewrite naming 10 gripper models from 6 manufacturers where the outgoing was looser prose. A LEGITIMATE WRITE THIS CHANGE WOULD REFUSE: ~4 a month fleet-wide on an 8-day window, against 724 wipes the retired axis waves through, with section_shrink_floor as a live-immediate hatch. Every other apparent refusal in that population spans a gap of 1,700s to 93 hours, and a slot absent that long was a DROP, which the guard declines to judge - so it is not a write the guard would ever have seen.

THE MINIMUM IS THE OTHER HALF. minShrinkGuardChars (500) was calibrated against CSS-inflated lengths; the same 500 on visible text leaves 587 of 1,079 slots unjudged. evaluateSectionShrink now takes the minimum as a PARAMETER - which section_visible_text.go's own header predicted in exactly that shape - and both callers pass minShrinkGuardVisibleChars = 200: scope 492 -> 959 of 1,079, with the guard-judged refusal count PINNED AT ONE at every step from 500 down to 50. 200 and not 120 because 200 is the deepest step the SECTION EDITOR's own population also covers (263 overwrite pairs: scope 153 -> 204, the same 4 refusals, all real hollowings), so that path moves on its own evidence rather than inheriting mine - which is the mistake 293 was filed to avoid, one parameter over. 500 and shrinkGuardTagStripper both STAY: their remaining consumer, load_current_section_content_action.go:262, is a pairing heuristic that refuses nothing, and re-tuning it would change which slots pair with no calibration covering that.

THE THIRD COPY, fixed rather than filed, and I expect this to be the contested part. The page-total content-regression guard was an anonymous block inlined in SavePageSectionsAction with hardcoded thresholds, no file, no test and NO escape hatch, making the same substitution - and worse for being a total, because a stylesheet anywhere props up the number every slot's loss is diluted into. [APPROXIMATE - paired slots only, not every deployed row, so weigh the ratio not the count]: across 366 pages it would allow a WHOLE-PAGE prose wipe on 337 (92%) where visible text refuses 363 of 363, and it refuses ZERO real rebuild writes on either axis. Extracted as enforcePageTotalTextFloor with page_total_text_floor (default 0.25 = today's behaviour, 0 disables; zero live consumers name it). The GUARANTEE is unchanged - refuse a near-wipe of the page - so this is a measure corrected toward its own stated intent, not new authority on a shared seam, and under the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 that is not architecture-scope. It also keeps failing OPEN on a measurement error exactly as the inline rule did, because making it fail closed like its two siblings is a separate behavioural question that deserves its own evidence. Leaving the blindest of three copies uncorrected inside the fix for "one call site of a shared judgement gets the rigorous fix, the sibling stays heuristic" (016b section 9) would have reproduced the defect being fixed, and the coverage test below could not have been written honestly with a live defect inside its own allow-list.

A SECOND DEFECT, found by tripping over it in my own harness. Slot names legitimately repeat on a page (LANDMINES.md: 11 of 17 duplicate groups are legitimate, generic-text-block 2-3x with differing content), and BOTH sides of this guard's comparison were maps keyed on name alone - m[ComponentName] = len on the incoming side, existing[slot] = len on the existing side - so on 14 pages the guard compared an ARBITRARY instance against an ARBITRARY instance, and which one won depended on DB row order and slice order. Now summed per name: bit-identical for the ~97% of groups with one instance, deterministic for the rest, more faithful than before (the insert loop writes EVERY instance, so last-write-wins undercounted what would actually be written), and it needs no assumption that position survives a rebuild. My first calibration join had the same wrong assumption and manufactured a refusal that does not exist; logged in WRONG_CALLS.md.

ANTI-DRIFT, and I rejected the obvious structural fix on purpose. Making evaluateSectionShrink take HTML and measure for itself would stop any caller choosing an axis - and would destroy the calibration harness, whose whole value is running BOTH axes through the REAL decision on real pairs. So the axis stays the caller's to supply and shrink_axis_coverage_test.go enforces it mechanically: a caller of evaluateSectionShrink that does not measure with visibleTextLength fails the build, as does a file applying the retired stripper without a reason in retiredAxisConsumers, with a vacuity control so a scan that matches nothing cannot pass. It also closes a hole found while writing it: the existing page_component_writer_coverage_test.go matches 'UPDATE page_components ... SET ... rendered_html =' and this path is DELETE+INSERT, so the fleet's highest-volume rendered_html writer was INVISIBLE to the fleet's writer-coverage test and unwiring a floor there failed nothing.

MUTATION-PROVEN, six mutations RUN before commit, not planned: (A) revert the per-slot axis -> 3 tests fail, in BOTH directions (the refusal test because the retired axis allows the poison, the repair test because it refuses the repair); (B) restore the 500 minimum -> the mid-sized-prose test fails, and nothing else in the suite could catch it because every other fixture is comfortably over 500 visible chars; (C) last-write-wins keying -> the repeated-slot test fails for one row ORDER and passes for the other, which is the finding; (D) revert the page-total axis -> it allows the whole-page wipe, proving that floor is load-bearing and not shadowed by its per-slot sibling; (E) unwire the page-total floor -> coverage fails; (F) put a caller back on the retired axis -> coverage fails twice. Whole actions package green at git archive HEAD.

The calibration harness itself is committed (shrink_axis_calibration_test.go, skipped unless SHRINK_CALIBRATION_JSONL names an export) because section_visible_text.go ends "RE-RUN THAT CALIBRATION before changing it" and until now nobody could: the run that justified the sibling's axis lived in one session's scratch directory and survives only as prose. A calibration a later reader cannot re-run is a claim, not evidence.

plan.summary: Correct the measurement axis of ALL THREE text floors on the page-save path to VISIBLE text (stylesheet and script content excluded), make evaluateSectionShrink's existing-side minimum a parameter and calibrate it to 200, extract the inlined page-total guard into a tested function with the config hatch it never had, sum per slot name instead of picking an arbitrary instance, and hold the axis with a coverage test so a fourth caller cannot pick a fourth axis.
plan.risks:
ROUND 2 ADDITIONS. The new item type save_guard_unmeasured has no automated consumer and no handler_agent, so a repeat is a new event rather than a failed fix (inherited from the emitter's recurrenceExpected) and it dedupes per page on its item key; it can therefore accumulate one row per affected page during a database incident, which is the intended signal and not a leak. The page-total floor STILL fails open — that is unchanged and deliberate. TestVisibleDefinitionsAgree's zero is measured on the archived populations, so it covers the content that exists rather than content a future writer might produce; it is a regression guard on the agreement, not a proof of it in general. TestEveryFloorEnforcerHasACaller reads SOURCE like its model, so it proves a call EXISTS, not that it executes, and it can be satisfied by a call in an unreachable branch.

MEASURED, one real false refusal: across the archived populations the visible axis would refuse exactly ONE write the guard would actually have judged (robot-hands.com/about/differentiators, 3,724->1,554 visible chars, hand-read as a legitimate tightening rewrite) - about 4 a month fleet-wide extrapolated from an 8-day window. A refusal blocks the WHOLE page save, which is the expensive failure mode, mitigated by section_shrink_floor / page_total_text_floor being live-immediate DB config needing no roll. SCOPE LOOSENING, measured: 120 of 1,079 rebuild pairs (11%) still fall below the 200-char minimum on visible text and leave the text floor's scope; the retired axis refused 0 of those and is structurally blind to prose deletion there, and the unchanged class-attribute floor (own minimum of 10 class attributes) still covers structural collapse on them. The page-total half's blindness figure is [APPROXIMATE] - measured over paired slots, not every deployed row, and the real guard filters on build_status='deployed', a different population; its false-refusal side IS exactly measured (0 of 366 pages on either axis). The summing change alters the unit of judgement on 14 pages from an arbitrary instance to the slot-name group, so instances individually under the minimum can aggregate over it (three 80-char blocks = 240) and come into scope. The page-total floor still fails OPEN on a measurement error, unlike its two siblings - carried over from the inline rule deliberately rather than changed unreviewed. Parsing cost: visible text needs a real HTML parse where the old rule used SQL REGEXP_REPLACE, so ~10KB x ~8 slots is now read into Go per save - the sibling class floor already fetches those exact rows and columns on every save of this action, so it is a second copy of an existing fetch, not a new class of cost.

edits.symbol: evaluateSectionShrink, minShrinkGuardVisibleChars, visibleIncomingBySlot, enforceSectionShrinkFloor, savePageSectionsUnmeasured, pageTotalUnmeasuredFix, incomingBySlot
edits.rationale: The axis change proper. evaluateSectionShrink gains minExistingChars (the shape section_visible_text.go's header predicted); the existing side stops measuring in SQL because REGEXP_REPLACE cannot exclude what is inside <style>; both sides sum per slot name instead of letting an arbitrary instance win; the refusal message names VISIBLE text so the operator knows which string was measured, which is also what makes a refusal greppable for post-roll verification. The retired stripper and the 500 constant STAY, annotated with their one remaining non-floor consumer, so nobody 'unifies' them. ROUND 2: (a) the page-total floor's FAIL-OPEN path now files a work item under its OWN type `save_guard_unmeasured` — not the refusal type its siblings use, because nothing was refused there and a row asserting otherwise is a false claim in a queue a human reads; producer set, key shape and 'no automated consumer' stated at the constructor per the 2026-08-02 §1 ruling. It still fails OPEN. (b) three `*IncomingBySlot` helpers collapse onto one `incomingBySlot(sections, measure)`: that duplication is HOW the last-write-wins keying defect came to exist in two of them independently, so the keying question is answered once and the measure is the parameter.

The third copy of the axis, extracted from an anonymous inline block so it has a home, a test and an escape hatch. It keeps its own population (build_status='deployed', NOT the agent-writable set) because the two floors answer different questions and folding them together would silently change one. It keeps failing OPEN, as the inline rule did - reconciling that with its siblings is a separate change. Its own aftermath sentence, because 'find why the writer regenerated that section' is the wrong question for a floor no single slot need have tripped.

edits.symbol: SavePageSectionsAction (the inline content-regression block, and the sections-reaching-save diagnostic)
edits.rationale: Replace the 30-line inline block with the call. And fix the diagnostic in the same commit: it advertised itself as 'the stripped-text total the regression guard will compute', which became FALSE the moment the floors moved to visible text - a diagnostic naming the wrong quantity is worse than none, because whoever debugs a refusal reads it as the guard's own arithmetic. It now logs both, which is what makes a refusal legible: this bug's signature is stripped GROWING while visible COLLAPSES.

Pass the shared minimum (500 -> 200 for this path too), with this path's OWN evidence quoted rather than mine. And correct its caller-census comment visibly: it asserted the whole-page path was 'unaffected by construction, not by convention', which was the weaker of two false claims - an axis that lives in the caller is not unaffected, it is UNGOVERNED, which is why that path went on counting stylesheets as prose for a fortnight after this one stopped.

What actually stops a fourth axis, chosen over a self-measuring decision function because that would destroy the calibration harness. Modelled on page_component_writer_coverage_test.go including its stated weakness (reads SOURCE: proves wiring EXISTS, not that it EXECUTES). Matches the CALL shrinkGuardTagStripper.ReplaceAllString( rather than the symbol name, so comments cannot trip it - the landmine about source-scanning tests making comments load-bearing is real and this file's own prose names the retired symbol repeatedly. Second test asserts the action still calls all three floors, which the existing writer-coverage test structurally cannot: its predicate is an UPDATE and this path is DELETE+INSERT. ROUND 2, editquality was right that 'closes a hole' overstated what ships — it does not generalise the older test's UPDATE-only regex, so a new writer on another DELETE+INSERT path stays invisible. Corrected to 'narrows' visibly in the header, and made partly true: TestEveryFloorEnforcerHasACaller fails when ANY enforce*Floor in the package has no caller at all, which is the generic case the claim was reaching for. MUT-293-H proves it bites.

The behavioural half: each guard driven against sqlmock, each assertion paired with a NAMED mutation that was RUN before commit. The 285 lane's own misstep was four tests that passed with the axis reverted because they exercised the helper and never the wiring. Includes both allow arms (the repair direction; an ordinary tightening rebuild) because a floor with no allow arm is indistinguishable from 'refuse everything', and fixture guards that fail if a fixture stops reproducing the trap - one of mine fired during development and it was testing the wrong quantity.

edits.rationale: The calibration itself, committed and re-runnable, because section_visible_text.go says 'RE-RUN THAT CALIBRATION before changing it' and the run that justified the sibling's axis lived in a scratch directory. It measures with the REAL functions, which is the trap that produced the earlier published figures (a regex approximation gave 2,754->68 for a pair that really reads 2,143->16, and a refusal count of 1 where the real code refuses 3). Skipped unless SHRINK_CALIBRATION_JSONL is set, so `go test ./...` is unaffected. The minimum being a parameter let me DELETE the sweep's replicated arithmetic and its pinning assertion - it now turns the real decision's own dial. ROUND 2, answering bug_historian's 'is visible defined once or three times' with a measurement rather than a code reading: the floor's notion of visible and the page assembler's sectionHasVisibleContent DIFFER by construction (parser vs regex, >=200 vs >10, opposite handling of code/pre and of entities), and only one direction matters — nothing this floor judges as prose-bearing may be droppable by the assembler. 6,585 in scope, ZERO droppable. A reading gives the same answer but cannot see the entity edge case, which is why it runs over the real population.
